notes.title: PUNT Development as of 11/25/16
notes.content:
The following is an article which was previously posted on Moddb, but is now being posted on Steam as well. Progress has been made since this article was originally posted.

Head Developer's twitter: [url=https://twitter.com/tristanh816]Twitter - Tristan .H[/url]

Corrupted Studios twitter: [url=https://twitter.com/CorruptedGames]Twitter - Corrupted Studios[/url]

Official Blog: [url=http://corruptedstudios.blogspot.com/]Blog[/url]

[img]https://ci4.googleusercontent.com/proxy/uCYF35IfldNOjYBOYioN8JxbUAKZpZbCe9Uqpf8OKKNlC1K9pokRZxrKt-lPvm9qN9NJgT9moCG2TV3pw9LBhz34TsRrYFcB-2As=s0-d-e1-ft#https://pbs.twimg.com/media/Cu_TSGzXEAAeAJY.jpg:large[/img]

For a week in October, I took a trip to Seattle with some members of rHetorical Studios for Steam Dev Days. While there, we showcased PUNT along side Alive & Kicking, and even allowed attendees to play the games and give their thoughts on the experience.

While there, we were also able to play multiple VR titles, tour Valve HQ, grab lunch with Jeep Barnett, and meet many other notable individuals. After playing PUNT and giving feedback, dev days attendees aided in guiding our work for weeks to come.

Our time in Washington helped us to establish multiple important contacts, both in and out of Valve. This networking paid off, as after conversations with multiple individuals, they've made very important contributions to PUNT's development, now allowing us to work on a more in depth Steam Workshop, Mac and Linux ports, and native Steam controller support, all of which wouldn't be possible without the generous help we've received from Valve and others. That all aside, time for actual game news!

For starters, we've switched engine branches once again. We're currently using a Alien Swarm based hybrid opposed to Source SDK 2013, but this will change in the near future to an alternative which we're currently unable to discuss publicly. This alternative is similar in nature to the ASW solution which we've made, but improves upon it in various areas and will allow for less restricted development of the game. Our engine changes have led to vastly improved shadows, lighting, particle systems, and more, all resulting in an increased graphical quality.

The following screenshots are puzzles from our Steam Dev Days demo maps and the most recent maps from the game's main campaign.

[url=http://media.moddb.com/images/members/3/2214/2213621/profile/20161103190846_1.jpg][img]http://media.moddb.com/images/members/3/2214/2213621/profile/20161103190846_1.jpg[/img][/url]

[url=http://media.moddb.com/images/members/3/2214/2213621/profile/20161103220743_1.jpg][img]http://media.moddb.com/images/members/3/2214/2213621/profile/20161103220743_1.jpg[/img][/url]

We've also been working to improve various aspects of mapping for PUNT, focusing on ease of use and convenience, all to make not only PUNT's development smoother, but to make mapping for the PUNT workshop easier in the future as well. We're also going to be focusing on game customization, and have been adding in game features such as customization for crosshairs, as well as possible punt gun customization in the future as well.

We've been extremely hard at work over the past two months, and we hope it's been shown as of late. Please leave any questions, comments or concerns, as we'd love hear what you have to say and will respond accordingly as soon as possible. Thank you all for your continued support, we all appreciate it.

Until next time,

-Tristan (BoxandRocks)
